data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old English name Oswald, which means 'divine power' or 'God's strength'. Oswald was a popular name among Anglo-Saxon and Norse rulers, including King Oswald of Northumbria. This name carries a rich historical and spiritual significance. The name Oswell carries the meaning “Divine strength, God's health” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Oswell usually hope their child will grow to embody divine strength, god's health and live with faith, good character and purpose.

The name, derived from Old English, embodied the blending of these cultural influences. The popularity of Oswald among these leaders showcased the power and strength of Christianity in their societies during a time when pagan practices dominated.

It reminds us of the power of faith and the strength that comes from relying on God.
